A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same efficient probing (EP) study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite retitling and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification benchmarks, computational-cost comparisons, localization analyses, ablations, and appendix low-shot and layer-wise experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds backbone evaluations, quantitative attention-complementarity analyses, and attention-mixing and Matryoshka experiments.

M1.justification: The main EP procedure and Equations 1–10 remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds auxiliary attention mixing through a linear-plus-softmax projection and Matryoshka variants using joint losses with shared nested or separate classifiers. These extend EP experimentally; attention mixing is explicitly excluded from the final design.

E1.justification: The SUN397 evaluation in v1 Figure 9f is absent from v2. The other seven classification datasets remain, including results relocated into the appendix. Newly evaluated generative backbones still perform image classification; they do not introduce generation tasks.

E2.justification: V2 explicitly adds MHCA to the reference comparisons, co-plotted with AIM in Figures 2–3, while retaining the existing named pooling methods. Table 5 also introduces a Vanilla Matryoshka comparison using separate classifiers. Newly added pretrained backbones are evaluation targets rather than competing probing algorithms.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation configurations for DiT, AIMv2, Franca, DINOv3 and DINOv2-L. New protocols match predictor counts for complementarity comparisons and test projected-map counts, multiple representation dimensions and Matryoshka loss weights. The established 90-epoch schedule, warmup, batch sizes and low-shot subsets remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative complementarity comparisons across backbones and probes, worst-pair redundancy measurements, checks across all 12 MAE blocks, and a cross-backbone entropy analysis. Appendix C.3 also tests attention mixing and Matryoshka tradeoffs. Existing projection ablations, dimensionality sweeps, low-shot and layer-wise analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, experimental error bars or significance tests. The retained standard-deviation attention maps summarize variation across heads, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial new results, including DiT LP/EP accuracy of 32.7/57.0 and complementarity, mixing and Matryoshka outcomes. DINO LP/EP entries change from 78.2/78.7 to 77.3/77.8; SigLIP and SigLIP2 LP change from 85.9/86.9 to 84.1/85.2, now explicitly labeled GAP. These revisions do not establish identical underlying settings. SUN397 results disappear, while low-shot and layer-wise values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The original attention derivations and complexity arguments are retained. V2 newly defines complementarity through one minus average or maximum off-diagonal cosine similarity and specifies joint Matryoshka losses. It adds no theorem or proof establishing why complementarity emerges.

C1.justification: The central claims about efficient probing, accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and broad applicability remain. V2 extends the framing to generative representations, claims greater attention complementarity than competing methods, and raises the stated maximum ImageNet gain from 13.6 to 24.3 points using DiT. The abstract's 10× speed-up claim is removed.

C2.justification: V2 interprets complementarity as potentially arising from attentive probing rather than solely backbone architecture, and connects diffuse backbone attention with larger EP gains. New Appendix D explicitly limits conclusions to frozen-backbone classification and characterizes the mechanism analysis as diagnostic. It also discusses untested fine-tuning interactions, structured tasks and multimodal extensions, while Section 4.2 clarifies that reported compute savings exclude the backbone.

D1.justification: V2 adds LUMI/AMD MI250X hardware information and discloses patch sizes, the Table 2 EP32 default, GAP-based LP entries and different-setting FT sources. Comparator descriptions gain detail, although Table 1 gives DELF softmax while its prose specifies softplus. V2 removes v1's explicit code-access link; this does not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens the research framing beyond its original MIM emphasis through discussion of vision-language, autoregressive and diffusion representations. Added connections include AIMv2, DiT/SiT, DINOv3, Franca and Matryoshka learning, alongside new support for fine-tuning cost arguments. Existing pooling, slot-attention and PEFT positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around broader representation evaluation. Preliminary method sections are merged, competitors move into experimental setup, analyses are regrouped, and implementation details move earlier in the appendix. Pooling-related work is relocated, and an appendix contents page and new concluding appendix sections are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column layout and extensively regroups benchmark panels between the main text and appendix. It adds an algorithm-comparison table, expands the pretraining-results table with parameter and gain columns, introduces complementarity and entropy plots and variant tables, and replaces the main attention visualization with color-coded maps across bird images. Many earlier appendix visualizations are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V1's complementarity argument relied mainly on qualitative maps; v2 adds quantitative comparisons, matched predictor counts and checks across all 12 MAE layers, substantially strengthening its evidential basis. Clearer FLOP and FT qualifications and explicit applicability limits also improve interpretation. The removed code pointer and new DELF table–prose inconsistency weaken reproducibility, but these limited drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger analysis.
